rows.question: Why did you leave Soho House?
rows.answer:
After about two and a half years, the role had stopped teaching me anything new. Soho House was a genuinely strong experience — high service standards, a demanding environment, daily work with members who expected you to already know what they needed. But toward the end I was executing well on something I'd already mastered.

What was pulling me was the technology and systems side of the industry. I'd seen first-hand how a badly handled PMS migration can destabilise a whole operation, and I wanted to be on that side of the problem — implementation, adoption, bridging product and real operations. Soho House wasn't going to offer that path.

No conflict, no abrupt exit — it was a deliberate move toward something different.
